summary: Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian and archaeologist. He held posts at the University of Oldenburg from around 1993 to 1997 and at Heidelberg University around 2003.

Bernfried Schlerath worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, having studied under Paul Thieme (~1950–1956). He held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (1956–1964), the University of Marburg (1964–1974), and the Free University of Berlin (1974–1992).
Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist. Succeeding Heinrich Lüders, he served as a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1937 to 1945.

Bernhard Forssman specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1956–1963) and held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics, studying at Vienna, Bonn, Charles University, Göttingen, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Vienna, the Tibetan-Iranian and Iranian Institutes, and Columbia University.

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at Zurich, Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp, Göttingen, and Paris. He held reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent posts at the University of Zurich between 1833 and 1845.

Bernhard Karlgren was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915). He later held academic posts at Uppsala University (~1915–1918) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne. His career included posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel University (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at NYU, Brooklyn Polytechnic, UCLA, and under Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers (1980).

Bert Vaux is a linguist who studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University. He held academic posts at Harvard University (1994–2003), the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (2003–2006), and the University of Cambridge (2006–2010).

Berthe Jansen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford, completing her doctorate under Jonathan A. Silk (2010), and held posts at Heidelberg University and Leiden University.

Berthold Delbrück worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, Rudolf Haym, Franz Bopp, and Heymann Steinthal. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1867–1870) and the University of Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer was a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied in Berlin and Leipzig, and held posts at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, and the Field Museum of Natural History.

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche II is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Bettina Bäumer works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, having studied at Salzburg, Vienna, Zurich, Rome, Munich, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. She held posts at Banaras Hindu University, the Alice Boner Institute, Vienna, and Abhinavagupta Research Library.

Bettine Birge works in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Columbia University and under Wm. Theodore de Bary, Wing-tsit Chan, and Masaaki Sugiyama, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Strasbourg, Kiel, Göttingen, Bonn, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg. She held posts at Kiel, Halle-Wittenberg, the University of Hamburg (1931–1933), the University of London, Oxford, and the University of Colombo (1945–1949).
Betty Jean Shefts is a scholar in linguistics, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Nornang.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (1962–1986), the University of Hyderabad, and the Institute for Advanced Study.
